targets.title: Morphological changes in secondary, but not primary, sensory cortex in individuals with life‐long olfactory sensory deprivation
targets.evidence_quote: First, a direct replication of our recent publication that demonstrated a surprising lack of morphological abnormalities in piriform cortex in individuals with CA compared to matched controls (Peter et al., 2020 ) was done using newly collected data ( n CA = 30, n Control = 30).
targets.outcome_quote: The replication results were near identical to the original study: bilateral clusters of group differences in the OFC, including CA atrophy around the olfactory sulci and volume increases in the medial orbital gyri. Importantly, no group differences in piriform cortex were detected.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report near-identical replication, including agreement on the null finding in piriform cortex.

reasoning: Newly collected imaging data and newly recruited controls re-test Peter et al. (2020). Thirteen CA participants overlap, but measurements were newly acquired and controls new. Subsequent multivariate extension pools old and new data; the central direct replication determines classification and verdict. Earlier conflicting studies are background in a chain, not additional targets.
